# zpftri

> Computes the inverse of a complex Hermitian positive definite matrix.

<section class="intro">

stored in Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zpftri from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zpftri';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zpftri( transr, uplo, N, A, strideA ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "conjugate-transpose"` | Specifies the storage format (`'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride length for `A` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: The Normal `TRANSR` of RFP A is stored;
  -   `= 'C'`: The Conjugate-transpose `TRANSR` of RFP A is stored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A in RFP format. RFP format is described by `TRANSR`, `UPLO`, and N as follows: If `TRANSR = 'N'` then RFP A is (0:N,0:k-1) when N is even; $k=N/2$. RFP A is (0:N-1,0:k) when N is odd; $k=N/2$. IF `TRANSR = 'C'` then RFP is the Conjugate-transpose of RFP A as defined when `TRANSR = 'N'`. The contents of RFP A are defined by `UPLO` as follows: If `UPLO = 'U'` the RFP A contains the nt elements of upper packed A. If `UPLO = 'L'` the RFP A contains the elements of lower packed A. The LDA of RFP A is (N+1)/2 when `TRANSR = 'C'`. When `TRANSR` is 'N' the LDA is N+1 when N is even and N is odd. See the Note below for more details.

  On exit, the Hermitian inverse of the original matrix, in the same storage format.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "conjugate-transpose", "no-transpose"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zpftri.ndarray( transr, uplo, N, A, strideA, offsetA ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "conjugate-transpose"` | Specifies the storage format (`'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride length for `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: The Normal `TRANSR` of RFP A is stored;
  -   `= 'C'`: The Conjugate-transpose `TRANSR` of RFP A is stored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A in RFP format. RFP format is described by `TRANSR`, `UPLO`, and N as follows: If `TRANSR = 'N'` then RFP A is (0:N,0:k-1) when N is even; $k=N/2$. RFP A is (0:N-1,0:k) when N is odd; $k=N/2$. IF `TRANSR = 'C'` then RFP is the Conjugate-transpose of RFP A as defined when `TRANSR = 'N'`. The contents of RFP A are defined by `UPLO` as follows: If `UPLO = 'U'` the RFP A contains the nt elements of upper packed A. If `UPLO = 'L'` the RFP A contains the elements of lower packed A. The LDA of RFP A is (N+1)/2 when `TRANSR = 'C'`. When `TRANSR` is 'N' the LDA is N+1 when N is even and N is odd. See the Note below for more details.

  On exit, the Hermitian inverse of the original matrix, in the same storage format.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "conjugate-transpose", "no-transpose"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the (i,i) element of the factor U or L is zero, and the inverse could not be computed.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zpftri()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZPFTRI`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zpftri.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zpftrf from '../../zpftrf/lib/index.js';
import zpftri from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zpftri';

// 3x3 HPD matrix in RFP format (TRANSR='no-transpose', UPLO='lower'):
const A = new Complex128Array([
	10.0,
	0.0,
	3.0,
	-1.0,
	1.0,
	2.0,
	6.0,
	0.0,
	8.0,
	0.0,
	2.0,
	-1.0
]);

// First, Cholesky-factorize the matrix:
let info = zpftrf( 'no-transpose', 'lower', 3, A, 1 );
console.log( 'zpftrf info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Then, compute the inverse:
info = zpftri( 'no-transpose', 'lower', 3, A, 1 );
console.log( 'zpftri info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'A (inverse in RFP):', reinterpret( A, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZPFTRI`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZPFTRI computes the inverse of a complex Hermitian positive definite matrix A using the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ computed by ZPFTRF.

### Further Details

We first consider Standard Packed Format when N is even. We give an example where $N = 6$.

```text
AP is Upper             AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04 05       00
   11 12 13 14 15       10 11
      22 23 24 25       20 21 22
         33 34 35       30 31 32 33
            44 45       40 41 42 43 44
               55       50 51 52 53 54 55
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:5,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(4:6,0:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the first three columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(1:6,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:2,0:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the last three columns of AP lower. To denote conjugate we place -- above the element. This covers the case N even and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
                        -- -- --
03 04 05                33 43 53
                           -- --
13 14 15                00 44 54
                              --
23 24 25                10 11 55
```

```text
33 34 35                20 21 22
--
00 44 45                30 31 32
-- --
01 11 55                40 41 42
-- -- --
02 12 22                50 51 52
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'C'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the conjugate- transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
-- -- -- --                -- -- -- -- -- --
03 13 23 33 00 01 02    33 00 10 20 30 40 50
-- -- -- -- --                -- -- -- -- --
04 14 24 34 44 11 12    43 44 11 21 31 41 51
-- -- -- -- -- --                -- -- -- --
05 15 25 35 45 55 22    53 54 55 22 32 42 52
```

We next consider Standard Packed Format when N is odd. We give an example where $N = 5$.

```text
AP is Upper                 AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04              00
   11 12 13 14              10 11
      22 23 24              20 21 22
         33 34              30 31 32 33
            44              40 41 42 43 44
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(3:4,0:1)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the first two columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:1,1:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the last two columns of AP lower. To denote conjugate we place -- above the element. This covers the case N odd and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
                           -- --
02 03 04                00 33 43
                              --
12 13 14                10 11 44
```

```text
22 23 24                20 21 22
--
00 33 34                30 31 32
-- --
01 11 44                40 41 42
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'C'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the conjugate- transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
-- -- --                   -- -- -- -- -- --
02 12 22 00 01             00 10 20 30 40 50
-- -- -- --                   -- -- -- -- --
03 13 23 33 11             33 11 21 31 41 51
-- -- -- -- --                   -- -- -- --
04 14 24 34 44             43 44 22 32 42 52
```

</section>
